3.0.0.en: The Apostle Peter makes clear that this is his second epistle, and that its purpose, together with the first epistle, is to remind them of God's commandments, to care for their spiritual life, and to remember the second coming of Christ. The kindness of the Apostle Peter appears in praising the readers of the epistle by describing their minds as pure, which encourages them to give attention to his words and to accept them.

3.1.0.en: The commandments with which the Apostle Peter reminds them are the teachings of the prophets in the Old Testament and the commandments of Christ in the New Testament.

3.1.1.en: Praise the one you are speaking to, so that you open his heart to hear your words, especially if it is a reproach or a rebuke, and know that words of praise, before they give rest to those who hear you, give rest and joy to you yourself.

3.2.s.en: (2) The denial of the second coming of Christ and the answer to it

3.2.0.en: He warns of the appearance of unbelieving people in the last days, by which he means the period from the days of Christ until His second coming; they are people immersed in their lusts, who scoff arrogantly at God and His Church.

3.3.0.en: These wicked people reject the idea of the second coming of Christ, on the evidence that the earth and all that is on it has remained steady over the years, so it will not perish or change as Christ said at His second coming; indeed all the fathers and forefathers have died and the earth and all that is on it has not changed.

3.4.0.en: The Apostle Peter answers those who do not believe in the coming of Christ with these proofs:

3.4.1.en: 1- Creation: the heavens and the earth did not exist, and God created them by His word out of the water that filled every place; then God divided between waters and waters and made the heavens above, and then caused the dry land to appear in the midst of the waters, and it became earth (Gen 1:9, 10); and as God created them, He is able to remove and change them at His second coming.

3.5.0.en: Whereby: the heavens and the earth.

3.5.1.en: 2- The Flood: the second proof of the coming of Christ and the change of the heavens and the earth is that in the days of the Flood the fountains of the great deep burst forth from the earth and the windows of heaven were opened with abundant rain, so that the whole world and humanity were drowned (Gen 7:11).

3.6.0.en: But the present heavens and earth will also be kept by the word of the Lord until the day of judgment, when God will destroy the ungodly.

3.7.0.en: 3- Time: he offers a third proof of the necessity of the second coming of Christ, which is that time for us as human beings is measured and we consider it short or long, so we say that many years have passed since the creation of the world and nothing has changed; but with God there is no time, rather a thousand years equal a day, as the same meaning is stated in the Psalm (Ps 90:4), and therefore His promise of His second coming will surely be fulfilled however long the time may be.

3.8.0.en: What people think is slowness on God's part, so that they doubted His word and its fulfillment, is in truth longsuffering on His part, to give a greater opportunity for repentance so that He may save all His children from destruction.

3.9.0.en: He declares an important truth, which is that the day of judgment will come suddenly, as a thief attacks to steal without anyone knowing the time of his attack. On that day there will be mighty sounds, which he calls a great noise, and the elements that compose the different materials will be dissolved and burn up, just as it was scientifically established in the twentieth century that the atom can be split. And the earth will burn, just as some nations have been able to cause huge fires with modern destructive bombs, and the heavens will burn, with the various planets they contain. By the heavens is not meant, of course, the throne of God, but the heaven of the planets.

3.9.1.en: Do not let your mind doubt the word of God, for faith is higher than reason. Try to understand with your mind, but do not oppose the word of God in the Holy Bible.

3.10.0.en: Since the heavens and the earth will be dissolved and changed, the Apostle calls us to prepare for the second coming of the Lord by the following:

3.10.1.en: 1- Holy conversation: that is, walking in righteousness and purity and carrying out God's commandments, knowing that our life is holy and consecrated to Him, so we are not occupied with the evils of the world.

3.11.0.en: 2- Longing for the Kingdom: because the heavens and the earth will burn, that is, pass away, we do not cling to material things but long to depart from the prison of the body, because we cannot be content with fellowship with Him on earth and yearn to enjoy permanent presence with Him in the Kingdom.

3.12.0.en: 3- Hope: although the world is full of evil and we strive to hold fast to righteousness amid its evils, we have hope in the Kingdom of Heaven, in which there is nothing but righteousness.

3.13.0.en: 4- Purity: we prepare by purifying our hearts from the attachments of the world, so that we gain inner peace and Christ dwells in us, in preparation for His permanent and complete dwelling in the Kingdom.

3.14.0.en: 5- Making use of life: our life is an opportunity that God gives us by His longsuffering to repent of our sins and do good in preparation for the Kingdom, as the Apostle Paul affirmed these same meanings so that we may prepare for the Kingdom (1 Thess 5:6), (1 Thess 4:13-18), (1 Cor 51-58).

3.15.0.en: The Apostle Peter points out that the epistles of the Apostle Paul contain philosophical statements that some wicked people distort and interpret wrongly, leading to the destruction of their souls; therefore it is necessary to adhere to the Church's interpretation of the epistles of Paul and of the whole Holy Bible, and no one should rush into an interpretation of his own, lest he go astray.

3.16.0.en: 6- Guarding against error: that is, the deviant teachings of the false teachers, and submission to the Church so that we stand firm in the upright faith that we learned and came to know from her.

3.17.0.en: 7- Spiritual growth: caring about spiritual growth in the knowledge of Christ through the Holy Bible and all the teachings of the Church, and experiencing Him through prayers, spiritual striving and service.

3.17.1.en: Remember always that you will leave this life, so prepare for eternity by caring for your prayers and readings every day, and if you sin, hasten to repentance, so that you enjoy the vision of God always.
